newsitem.title: UK: UK favourite to win S. Africa arms deal - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: UK favourite to win S. Africa arms deal - newspaper.

text.p: LONDON, March 31 - Britain is favourite to win an international competition to sell training aircraft, frigates and radar to South Africa, according to the London Sunday Times.

The newspaper said British Aerospace Plc (BAE) and General Electric Co Plc (GEC) would be the main beneficiaries of the deal, estimated to be worth between 1.5 billion and 2.0 billion pounds ($2.45-3.27 billion).
Asked for comment, a BAE spokesman on Monday said only:"South Africa is a place where we have a big marketing presence."

The Sunday Times report, which quoted "industry experts", said the main elements in the deal would be BAE Hawk fighter trainers, frigates made by GEC and radar from GEC's Marconi electronics division.
It said the deal would involve significant manufacture in South Africa through cooperation with local companies. A final decision on the deal was expected in the next few months.
